rows.title: CT officials focus on tax cuts as new election cycle starts
rows.standfirst: With the next election less than 12 months away, the 2026 General Assembly session could be swamped with tax-cutting ideas from both parties.

rows.title: 3 CT state employee unions to get pay hikes worth 4.5%
rows.standfirst: The COLA and step raise effectively represent a 4.5% increase and could help all state employees get similar raises.

rows.title: Borrowing for transportation on Lamont chopping block
rows.standfirst: Stagnant fuel and sales tax revenues mean CT will have to roll back plans to boost transportation borrowing, according to a new report.

rows.title: Lamont: CT savings habits are paying big dividends
rows.standfirst: Officials said next year’s pension payment would have been $857 million more if CT hadn’t put $10 billion into its pensions in recent years.

rows.title: Analysis shows CT ready for next recession as never before
rows.standfirst: A new forecast from Gov. Ned Lamont’s administration projects a moderate downturn wouldn’t drain state reserves for two and a half years.

rows.title: Should CT fund its own SNAP program? Lamont, budget chair disagree
rows.standfirst: The proposed state-funded SNAP program would be for those expected to lose federal benefits by March 31. Gov. Ned Lamont isn’t on board.

rows.title: Lamont pitches millions for food pantries, Planned Parenthood
rows.standfirst: Lamont announces $168 million to offset federal cuts to nutrition assistance, reproductive health services and health insurance.

rows.title: Waterbury nonprofit used LIHEAP funds to pay its expenses
rows.standfirst: CT officials moved to take control of New Opportunities Inc. after it bounced a $1.5M check and acknowledged using federal energy assistance to cover its costs.
